items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 809-811: a mere proposition is equivalent to its truncation. The proof (source lines 812-816) is short but it is a construction rather than a pointer: one direction is the projection, the other is the universal property of the truncation applied to the identity map, and that application is exactly where the hypothesis that P is a mere proposition is consumed; the two maps are then recognised as quasi-inverses by a cited criterion. Identifying the two maps and seeing which hypothesis licenses the extension is the substance, and the statement alone shows none of it.
